questions.stem: Which statement best reflects current National Kidney Foundation guidance about NSAID use in chronic kidney disease?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Daily NSAID use deserves review because long-term exposure can reduce renal blood flow and increase kidney risk in CKD.","B":"Daily NSAID use is preferred in CKD because these medicines increase renal blood flow and protect kidney function.","C":"Over-the-counter NSAIDs have minimal kidney risk in CKD because nonprescription status indicates long-term renal safety.","D":"Higher NSAID doses are safer in CKD because stronger anti-inflammatory effects reduce the chance of renal injury."}}
questions.rationale: The National Kidney Foundation states that NSAIDs can lower the amount of blood flowing to the kidneys and can cause kidney damage, especially at higher doses or with long-term use. Option A accurately reflects that guidance. Options B and D incorrectly describe NSAIDs as renally protective, and Option C incorrectly treats nonprescription status as evidence of long-term renal safety.
questions.source_name: National Kidney Foundation — Safe Medicine Use with Chronic Kidney Disease
questions.source_detail: Current NKF guidance states that NSAIDs can lower renal blood flow and cause kidney damage, especially with high doses or long-term use; this is particularly relevant for people living with CKD.

qc.qc_note: Strict final audit: max/min option-character ratio <=1.15; keyed option within 10% of distractor mean; keyed option is neither shortest nor longest; distractors manually reviewed for clinical plausibility, grammatical parallelism, and answer-cue leakage.
